content: For patients who do not have a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), heart failure (HF), or chronic kidney disease (CKD), the selection of antidiabetic medications should prioritize their effectiveness in achieving personalized blood glucose targets and weight management goals. Additionally, the choice of medication should take into account the potential side effects, particularly the risks of hypoglycemia and weight changes, as well as the cost of the medication and the patient’s individual preferences. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GIP/GLP-1 RAs) have demonstrated significant efficacy in reducing hemoglobin A1C levels and promoting weight loss. Furthermore, newer formulations of these medications have shown sustained effects over time and high levels of therapeutic efficacy.
